tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

schema.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

Ask the user to run each in a separate session (ideally a different LLM) and paste back the findings. When findings are pasted, treat them as those layers' findings and resume from this point. This is the only allowed parent-side read of a reviewer instruction file.

4. **Layer failure handling**: If any layer fails, times out, or returns empty results, append the layer's `name` to `{failed_layers}` (comma-separated) and proceed with findings from the remaining layers.

5. Collect all findings from the completed layers, keeping track of each finding's originating layer `id`.

37	+# Epic 3 Context: Multimodal Capture & Processing
38	+
39	+<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->
40	+
41	+## Goal
42	+
43	+Users capture a journal Entry through one shared Insertion Modal in three ways — typed text, recorded audio, or a photo — and every modality ends up as the same persisted `Entry` shape. Audio is transcribed entirely on-device; a photo's text is recognized server-side via OCR before the Entry exists. Text and audio/photo stay merged into one epic because an un-transcribed audio Entry or un-OCR'd photo Entry is not a usable product outcome on its own — "capture" and "process" are one milestone here, not two. The epic also guarantees interrupting any capture (switching tabs, backing out, stopping early) never leaves a stray partial or empty Entry behind. This is the first epic to introduce `features/entries/`, which every later epic that creates or reads an Entry (Timeline, Search, Chat save-to-journal) will consume through its port — so decisions made here about that port's shape are load-bearing for the rest of the app.
44	+
45	+## Stories
46	+
47	+- Story 3.1: Text Entry Capture & Insertion Modal Shell
48	+- Story 3.2: Audio Entry Capture & On-Device Transcription
49	+- Story 3.3: Photo Entry Capture & Backend OCR
50	+- Story 3.4: Cancel-Safe Capture Across All Tabs
51	+
52	+## Requirements & Constraints
53	+
54	+- All three capture modalities (text, audio, photo) must produce the same persisted Entry shape; `source` is `manual`/`audio`/`photo` respectively, and each `POST /entries` call must carry the correct one.
55	+- Audio and photo Entries are only "complete" once processed: audio via on-device transcription, photo via backend OCR. The transcribed/recognized text is editable before the user taps Salvar; the Entry is only created on explicit save, not automatically after processing finishes.
56	+- Audio transcription runs 100% on-device via `whisper_ggml`; no call in this pipeline may ever contain audio bytes. The audio pipeline has exactly four states in sequence: recording → processing → transcribed → (on failure) error with retry; the recorded media is never discarded on a transcription failure.
57	+- Photo OCR calls the backend before the Entry is created, mirroring the same four-state shape: capture → processing OCR → recognized → error. `OCR_NO_TEXT` is a distinct, non-retryable outcome with two recovery paths: "Tentar novamente" (retry OCR on the same photo) and "Salvar só a foto" (save with no extracted text) — never a single generic failure message. An oversized photo returns non-retryable `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` (413); show a size-specific message with no retry button.
58	+- Cancel-safety (FR-11) is absolute: interrupting a capture before Salvar — closing the modal, switching Insertion Modal tabs, backing out mid-photo, stopping a recording early — must never fire `POST /entries`. Opening the modal always resets all three tabs to idle/empty; switching tabs mid-capture cancels the in-flight capture outright (resolved ambiguity — the prototype itself left this undefined).
59	+- Offline: the "+" entry point is disabled with the same offline-banner treatment as chat send. Capture requires a live `POST /entries` round trip (PII check + embedding), so there is no local-only queued write — a write attempted with no connectivity resolves immediately to `NetworkOffline`, never queued.
60	+- Every screen-reader-relevant state transition needs an announced label ("Gravando," "Transcrevendo," "Erro ao transcrever, toque para tentar novamente," etc.) — color/animation alone never carries state.
61	+
62	+## Technical Decisions
63	+
64	+- Two feature modules split the work: `features/entries/` owns the `Entry` entity, the `EntriesRepository` port (`create` + `read` only — no update/delete ever), and the entries `hive_ce` box. `features/capture/` owns the Insertion Modal UI, the on-device Whisper STT flow, and the OCR call, and holds no Entry data itself — it only consumes the abstract port from `entries/domain` (never imports `entries/data/` or `entries/presentation/`). This port is exactly what RF10 (Epic 6, save chat message as entry) and RF06/RF07 (Search, Timeline) will extend/reuse later — get its shape right here, not provisionally.
65	+- `create` on the port is idempotent on `(origin, chatMessageId)`, though that specific guard only matters starting with RF10; this epic just needs to not violate the port's shape.
66	+- Backend calls for this epic: `POST /entries` → function `entries-create`; `POST /media/ocr` → function `media-ocr` (the photo itself is not persisted server-side, only the extracted text comes back). Both calls follow the standard header rules (`apikey` always, `Authorization: Bearer <user token>`, since neither operation is one of the three `security: []` exceptions).
67	+- Error handling: map the 13 backend error codes (plus the local-only `MalformedResponse`) to the one sealed `Failure` hierarchy already defined in `core/failure/`. For this epic specifically: `OcrNoText` and `PayloadTooLarge` are both non-retryable and need their own distinct UI treatment, not a generic error state. The retry interceptor fires only for the 6 server `retryable:true` codes — OCR/payload failures are never auto-retried.
68	+- The capture feature defines its own sealed state class for its multi-step audio/OCR state machines — it is explicitly excluded from using the shared generic `Resource<T>` type (`Resource<T>` is reserved for RF06/RF09's simpler single-fetch screens).
69	+- The Insertion Modal's three tabs are internal states of one bottom sheet, never nested sheets; its entrance animation is the shared `sheetUp` (0.2s) choreography, with no other motion invented.
70	+
71	+## UX & Interaction Patterns
72	+
73	+- Insertion Modal: three equal-width tabs (Texto/Áudio/Foto); only the active tab gets a filled `colorPrimary` background. A close ("x") control is always present. The modal opens on Texto by default.
74	+- Audio tab: an animated multi-bar waveform with a monospace running timer while recording; on stop, the waveform freezes at 35% opacity with a "Transcrevendo..." label while processing (no spinner needed beyond that). Once transcribed, text is editable and "Salvar" enables; the original audio duration shows in monospace.
75	+- Photo tab: thumbnail + spinner + "Reconhecendo texto..." while OCR runs. Once recognized, text is editable before Salvar.
76	+- Dynamic Type and tap-target rules (≥44pt, no truncation at largest accessibility text size) apply to all controls built here, same as everywhere else in the app.
77	+- Reduce Motion: this epic has no cursor-blink (that's Chat), but still must honor the `sheetUp`/`scrimIn`-only animation rule and skip it when Reduce Motion is on.
78	+
79	+## Cross-Story Dependencies
80	+
81	+- Story 3.1 is the first consumer of `features/entries/` and must stand up the `Entry` entity, `EntriesRepository` port (`create`), and the entries Hive box — Stories 3.2 and 3.3 build on top of this rather than creating their own local Entry model.
82	+- Story 3.4 (cancel-safety) is a cross-cutting rule that applies to the tab/state machines built in 3.1–3.3; it's written as its own story but has no independent UI surface — it hardens behavior already present in the other three.
83	+- This epic depends on Epic 2 (Biometric Vault): the Insertion Modal is only reachable once the vault is unlocked.
84	+- Everything this epic builds in `features/entries/` is a hard dependency for Epic 4 (Timeline), Epic 5 (Search), and Epic 6's RF10 (save-to-journal) — those epics extend this port rather than replacing it.

407	+/// The Insertion Modal's 3 tabs — Boundaries: "3 equal-width tabs (Texto/
408	+/// Áudio/Foto)". Only [texto] is functional this story; [audio]/[foto]
409	+/// render idle, non-interactive placeholders (Stories 3.2/3.3).
410	+enum CaptureTab { texto, audio, foto }
411	+
412	+/// Capture's own state for the Insertion Modal — never the shared
413	+/// `Resource<T>` (Boundaries). A sealed class, not `freezed` (no codegen
414	+/// for this story beyond `entry_dto.g.dart`, Verification): every
415	+/// variant always carries the common [activeTab]/[text] so switching tabs
416	+/// or typing never needs to know which variant it's coming from.
417	+sealed class TextEntryState {
418	+  const TextEntryState({required this.activeTab, required this.text});
419	+
420	+  final CaptureTab activeTab;
421	+  final String text;
422	+}
423	+
424	+/// Ready to type/save — the state immediately after the modal opens
425	+/// (Boundaries: "Opens on Texto, all 3 tabs idle/empty"), after a tab
426	+/// switch, and after a keystroke.
427	+class TextEntryIdle extends TextEntryState {
428	+  const TextEntryIdle({required super.activeTab, required super.text});
429	+}
430	+
431	+/// Salvar tapped, `POST /entries` in flight — the I/O matrix's "no
432	+/// auto-retry, no double-submit": `InsertionModal` disables Salvar/the
433	+/// text field for the duration of this state.
434	+class TextEntrySaving extends TextEntryState {
435	+  const TextEntrySaving({required super.activeTab, required super.text});
436	+}
437	+
438	+/// The save attempt succeeded — `InsertionModal`'s listener reacts to
439	+/// this by popping the sheet (I/O matrix: "success closes the modal").
440	+/// Terminal: nothing meaningful follows it for this cubit instance, since
441	+/// the modal (and the factory-scoped cubit backing it) is already
442	+/// closing.
443	+class TextEntrySaved extends TextEntryState {
444	+  const TextEntrySaved({required super.activeTab, required super.text});
445	+}
446	+
447	+/// The last save attempt failed (incl. offline, via the existing
448	+/// `Failure.networkOffline`) — [message] is `Failure.message` verbatim
449	+/// (I/O matrix: "Inline message from `Failure.message`"); Salvar is
450	+/// re-enabled, the modal stays open, no auto-retry.
451	+class TextEntryError extends TextEntryState {
452	+  const TextEntryError({
453	+    required super.activeTab,
454	+    required super.text,
455	+    required this.message,
456	+  });
457	+
458	+  final String message;
459	+}
460	+
461	+/// Drives `InsertionModal`. Calls [EntriesRepository.create] directly on
462	+/// [save] — no use-case layer, matching this codebase's existing
463	+/// convention (Design Notes: `AccountSettingsCubit`/`AuthCubit`). A fresh,
464	+/// `get_it`-factory-scoped instance per "+" tap (Boundaries: "Modal open
465	+/// resets") — starting state is always [TextEntryIdle] on
466	+/// [CaptureTab.texto] with empty text, so no explicit reset method is
467	+/// needed the way `AccountSettingsCubit.clearStaleError()` needs one for
468	+/// its own long-lived singleton.
469	+class TextEntryCubit extends Cubit<TextEntryState> {
470	+  TextEntryCubit(this._repository)
471	+    : super(const TextEntryIdle(activeTab: CaptureTab.texto, text: ''));
472	+
473	+  final EntriesRepository _repository;
474	+
475	+  /// Switches the active tab, preserving whatever Texto text was already
476	+  /// typed (Never: the full cross-tab cancel-safety rule is Story 3.4's
477	+  /// scope — this story's trivial case just needs the tab itself to
478	+  /// switch without losing in-progress text or firing any `create` call).
479	+  ///
480	+  /// Review finding: ignored while [TextEntrySaving] — `InsertionModal`
481	+  /// already disables the tab bar for that case, but this is the
482	+  /// authoritative guard regardless of how `selectTab` is invoked. Without
483	+  /// it, switching away mid-save would still let `save()`'s eventual
484	+  /// `TextEntrySaved`/`TextEntryError` emission land on top of whatever
485	+  /// tab/text the user has since moved to — popping the modal
486	+  /// unexpectedly, or showing an error against an unrelated tab.
487	+  void selectTab(CaptureTab tab) {
488	+    if (tab == state.activeTab || state is TextEntrySaving) {
489	+      return;
490	+    }
491	+    emit(TextEntryIdle(activeTab: tab, text: state.text));
492	+  }
493	+
494	+  /// Mirrors the Texto field's own `TextEditingController` into this
495	+  /// cubit's state, so [save] has the latest typed text to send. Ignored
496	+  /// while a save is already in flight — the field is disabled in that
497	+  /// state (`InsertionModal`), so this should never fire then regardless.
498	+  void updateText(String text) {
499	+    if (state is TextEntrySaving) {
500	+      return;
501	+    }
502	+    emit(TextEntryIdle(activeTab: state.activeTab, text: text));
503	+  }

510	+  /// the authoritative guard regardless of how `save()` is invoked.
511	+  Future<void> save() async {
512	+    final text = state.text.trim();
513	+    if (text.isEmpty || state is TextEntrySaving) {
514	+      return;
515	+    }
516	+    final activeTab = state.activeTab;

533	+      (_) => emit(TextEntrySaved(activeTab: activeTab, text: text)),
534	+    );
535	+  }
536	+}

554	+/// from the Home/Chat "+" control (`placeholder_screens.dart`). Only
555	+/// Texto is functional this story (Boundaries) — Áudio/Foto each render
556	+/// their own idle, non-interactive placeholder (Stories 3.2/3.3).
557	+class InsertionModal extends StatelessWidget {
558	+  const InsertionModal({required this.cubit, super.key});
559	+
560	+  final TextEntryCubit cubit;
561	+
562	+  /// Presents the modal exactly as the Boundaries dictate:
563	+  /// `showModalBottomSheet(isScrollControlled: true, barrierColor:
564	+  /// colorScrimHeavy)`, `radiusLg` top corners + `elevation2` (drawn by
565	+  /// this widget's own `Container`, not Material's `elevation` double —
566	+  /// same convention `ConfirmationDialog`'s card already uses), and a
567	+  /// `durationSheetUp` entrance that collapses to zero under Reduce
568	+  /// Motion (`MediaQuery.disableAnimations`).
569	+  ///
570	+  /// [cubit] is a fresh, `get_it`-factory-scoped instance — one per "+"
571	+  /// tap (Boundaries: "Modal open resets"), closed here once the sheet is
572	+  /// gone, regardless of how it closed (Salvar success, "x", swipe-down,
573	+  /// or barrier dismiss) — the caller never has to remember to do this
574	+  /// itself.
575	+  static Future<void> show(
576	+    BuildContext context, {
577	+    required TextEntryCubit cubit,
578	+  }) async {
579	+    final reduceMotion = MediaQuery.of(context).disableAnimations;
580	+    final controller =
581	+        BottomSheet.createAnimationController(Navigator.of(context))
582	+          ..duration = reduceMotion
583	+              ? Duration.zero
584	+              : DesignTokens.durationSheetUp
585	+          // Boundaries only names the entrance, but Reduce Motion should
586	+          // collapse the exit the same way — otherwise dismissing the
587	+          // sheet would still animate for anyone who asked for no motion.
588	+          ..reverseDuration = reduceMotion ? Duration.zero : null;
589	+    try {
590	+      await showModalBottomSheet<void>(
591	+        context: context,
592	+        isScrollControlled: true,
593	+        barrierColor: DesignTokens.colorScrimHeavy,
594	+        backgroundColor: Colors.transparent,
595	+        elevation: 0,
596	+        transitionAnimationController: controller,
597	+        builder: (_) => InsertionModal(cubit: cubit),
598	+      );
599	+    } finally {
600	+      // `showModalBottomSheet`'s own Future completes as soon as the
601	+      // route is popped — *before* the exit (`reverse()`) animation the
602	+      // framework drives on this same controller actually finishes.
603	+      // Disposing immediately would cancel that animation's ticker
604	+      // mid-flight, permanently freezing the sheet on screen (its
605	+      // `AnimatedBuilder` keeps rendering the controller's last value,
606	+      // and the route itself never reaches `AnimationStatus.dismissed`
607	+      // to be removed from the `Overlay`). Documented behavior
608	+      // (`BottomSheet.transitionAnimationController`'s own doc: "the
609	+      // caller is responsible for disposing it when the controller is
610	+      // no longer needed") — waiting for `dismissed` first is that
611	+      // "no longer needed" point.
612	+      if (!controller.isDismissed) {
613	+        final animationDone = Completer<void>();
614	+        void onStatusChange(AnimationStatus status) {
615	+          if (status == AnimationStatus.dismissed) {
616	+            animationDone.complete();
617	+          }
618	+        }
619	+
620	+        controller.addStatusListener(onStatusChange);
621	+        await animationDone.future;
622	+        controller.removeStatusListener(onStatusChange);
623	+      }
624	+      controller.dispose();
625	+      await cubit.close();
626	+    }
627	+  }
628	+
629	+  @override
630	+  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
631	+    return BlocProvider.value(value: cubit, child: const _InsertionModalBody());

+# Epic 3 Context: Multimodal Capture & Processing
+
+<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->
+
+## Goal
+
+Users capture a journal Entry through one shared Insertion Modal in three ways — typed text, recorded audio, or a photo — and every modality ends up as the same persisted `Entry` shape. Audio is transcribed entirely on-device; a photo's text is recognized server-side via OCR before the Entry exists. Text and audio/photo stay merged into one epic because an un-transcribed audio Entry or un-OCR'd photo Entry is not a usable product outcome on its own — "capture" and "process" are one milestone here, not two. The epic also guarantees interrupting any capture (switching tabs, backing out, stopping early) never leaves a stray partial or empty Entry behind. This is the first epic to introduce `features/entries/`, which every later epic that creates or reads an Entry (Timeline, Search, Chat save-to-journal) will consume through its port — so decisions made here about that port's shape are load-bearing for the rest of the app.
+
+## Stories
+
+- Story 3.1: Text Entry Capture & Insertion Modal Shell
+- Story 3.2: Audio Entry Capture & On-Device Transcription
+- Story 3.3: Photo Entry Capture & Backend OCR
+- Story 3.4: Cancel-Safe Capture Across All Tabs
+
+## Requirements & Constraints
+
+- All three capture modalities (text, audio, photo) must produce the same persisted Entry shape; `source` is `manual`/`audio`/`photo` respectively, and each `POST /entries` call must carry the correct one.
+- Audio and photo Entries are only "complete" once processed: audio via on-device transcription, photo via backend OCR. The transcribed/recognized text is editable before the user taps Salvar; the Entry is only created on explicit save, not automatically after processing finishes.
+- Audio transcription runs 100% on-device via `whisper_ggml`; no call in this pipeline may ever contain audio bytes. The audio pipeline has exactly four states in sequence: recording → processing → transcribed → (on failure) error with retry; the recorded media is never discarded on a transcription failure.
+- Photo OCR calls the backend before the Entry is created, mirroring the same four-state shape: capture → processing OCR → recognized → error. `OCR_NO_TEXT` is a distinct, non-retryable outcome with two recovery paths: "Tentar novamente" (retry OCR on the same photo) and "Salvar só a foto" (save with no extracted text) — never a single generic failure message. An oversized photo returns non-retryable `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` (413); show a size-specific message with no retry button.
+- Cancel-safety (FR-11) is absolute: interrupting a capture before Salvar — closing the modal, switching Insertion Modal tabs, backing out mid-photo, stopping a recording early — must never fire `POST /entries`. Opening the modal always resets all three tabs to idle/empty; switching tabs mid-capture cancels the in-flight capture outright (resolved ambiguity — the prototype itself left this undefined).
+- Offline: the "+" entry point is disabled with the same offline-banner treatment as chat send. Capture requires a live `POST /entries` round trip (PII check + embedding), so there is no local-only queued write — a write attempted with no connectivity resolves immediately to `NetworkOffline`, never queued.
+- Every screen-reader-relevant state transition needs an announced label ("Gravando," "Transcrevendo," "Erro ao transcrever, toque para tentar novamente," etc.) — color/animation alone never carries state.
+
+## Technical Decisions
+
+- Two feature modules split the work: `features/entries/` owns the `Entry` entity, the `EntriesRepository` port (`create` + `read` only — no update/delete ever), and the entries `hive_ce` box. `features/capture/` owns the Insertion Modal UI, the on-device Whisper STT flow, and the OCR call, and holds no Entry data itself — it only consumes the abstract port from `entries/domain` (never imports `entries/data/` or `entries/presentation/`). This port is exactly what RF10 (Epic 6, save chat message as entry) and RF06/RF07 (Search, Timeline) will extend/reuse later — get its shape right here, not provisionally.
+- `create` on the port is idempotent on `(origin, chatMessageId)`, though that specific guard only matters starting with RF10; this epic just needs to not violate the port's shape.
+- Backend calls for this epic: `POST /entries` → function `entries-create`; `POST /media/ocr` → function `media-ocr` (the photo itself is not persisted server-side, only the extracted text comes back). Both calls follow the standard header rules (`apikey` always, `Authorization: Bearer <user token>`, since neither operation is one of the three `security: []` exceptions).
+- Error handling: map the 13 backend error codes (plus the local-only `MalformedResponse`) to the one sealed `Failure` hierarchy already defined in `core/failure/`. For this epic specifically: `OcrNoText` and `PayloadTooLarge` are both non-retryable and need their own distinct UI treatment, not a generic error state. The retry interceptor fires only for the 6 server `retryable:true` codes — OCR/payload failures are never auto-retried.
+- The capture feature defines its own sealed state class for its multi-step audio/OCR state machines — it is explicitly excluded from using the shared generic `Resource<T>` type (`Resource<T>` is reserved for RF06/RF09's simpler single-fetch screens).
+- The Insertion Modal's three tabs are internal states of one bottom sheet, never nested sheets; its entrance animation is the shared `sheetUp` (0.2s) choreography, with no other motion invented.
+
+## UX & Interaction Patterns
+
+- Insertion Modal: three equal-width tabs (Texto/Áudio/Foto); only the active tab gets a filled `colorPrimary` background. A close ("x") control is always present. The modal opens on Texto by default.
+- Audio tab: an animated multi-bar waveform with a monospace running timer while recording; on stop, the waveform freezes at 35% opacity with a "Transcrevendo..." label while processing (no spinner needed beyond that). Once transcribed, text is editable and "Salvar" enables; the original audio duration shows in monospace.
+- Photo tab: thumbnail + spinner + "Reconhecendo texto..." while OCR runs. Once recognized, text is editable before Salvar.
+- Dynamic Type and tap-target rules (≥44pt, no truncation at largest accessibility text size) apply to all controls built here, same as everywhere else in the app.
+- Reduce Motion: this epic has no cursor-blink (that's Chat), but still must honor the `sheetUp`/`scrimIn`-only animation rule and skip it when Reduce Motion is on.
+
+## Cross-Story Dependencies
+
+- Story 3.1 is the first consumer of `features/entries/` and must stand up the `Entry` entity, `EntriesRepository` port (`create`), and the entries Hive box — Stories 3.2 and 3.3 build on top of this rather than creating their own local Entry model.
+- Story 3.4 (cancel-safety) is a cross-cutting rule that applies to the tab/state machines built in 3.1–3.3; it's written as its own story but has no independent UI surface — it hardens behavior already present in the other three.
+- This epic depends on Epic 2 (Biometric Vault): the Insertion Modal is only reachable once the vault is unlocked.
+- Everything this epic builds in `features/entries/` is a hard dependency for Epic 4 (Timeline), Epic 5 (Search), and Epic 6's RF10 (save-to-journal) — those epics extend this port rather than replacing it.

+/// Registers the `capture` feature into the project's single `get_it`
+/// instance (`sl`). Unlike every other feature's cubit in this codebase

+    () => TextEntryCubit(sl<EntriesRepository>()),

index 0000000..e511619
--- /dev/null
+++ b/lib/features/capture/presentation/cubit/text_entry_cubit.dart
@@ -0,0 +1,135 @@
+import 'package:flutter_bloc/flutter_bloc.dart';
+
+import '../../../entries/domain/entities/entry.dart';
+import '../../../entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart';
+
+/// The Insertion Modal's 3 tabs — Boundaries: "3 equal-width tabs (Texto/
+/// Áudio/Foto)". Only [texto] is functional this story; [audio]/[foto]
+/// render idle, non-interactive placeholders (Stories 3.2/3.3).
+enum CaptureTab { texto, audio, foto }
+
+/// Capture's own state for the Insertion Modal — never the shared
+/// `Resource<T>` (Boundaries). A sealed class, not `freezed` (no codegen
+/// for this story beyond `entry_dto.g.dart`, Verification): every
+/// variant always carries the common [activeTab]/[text] so switching tabs
+/// or typing never needs to know which variant it's coming from.
+sealed class TextEntryState {
+  const TextEntryState({required this.activeTab, required this.text});
+
+  final CaptureTab activeTab;
+  final String text;
+}
+
+/// Ready to type/save — the state immediately after the modal opens
+/// (Boundaries: "Opens on Texto, all 3 tabs idle/empty"), after a tab
+/// switch, and after a keystroke.
+class TextEntryIdle extends TextEntryState {
+  const TextEntryIdle({required super.activeTab, required super.text});
+}
+
+/// Salvar tapped, `POST /entries` in flight — the I/O matrix's "no
+/// auto-retry, no double-submit": `InsertionModal` disables Salvar/the
+/// text field for the duration of this state.
+class TextEntrySaving extends TextEntryState {
+  const TextEntrySaving({required super.activeTab, required super.text});
+}
+
+/// The save attempt succeeded — `InsertionModal`'s listener reacts to
+/// this by popping the sheet (I/O matrix: "success closes the modal").
+/// Terminal: nothing meaningful follows it for this cubit instance, since
+/// the modal (and the factory-scoped cubit backing it) is already
+/// closing.
+class TextEntrySaved extends TextEntryState {
+  const TextEntrySaved({required super.activeTab, required super.text});
+}
+
+/// The last save attempt failed (incl. offline, via the existing
+/// `Failure.networkOffline`) — [message] is `Failure.message` verbatim
+/// (I/O matrix: "Inline message from `Failure.message`"); Salvar is
+/// re-enabled, the modal stays open, no auto-retry.
+class TextEntryError extends TextEntryState {
+  const TextEntryError({
+    required super.activeTab,
+    required super.text,
+    required this.message,
+  });
+
+  final String message;
+}
+
+/// Drives `InsertionModal`. Calls [EntriesRepository.create] directly on
+/// [save] — no use-case layer, matching this codebase's existing
+/// convention (Design Notes: `AccountSettingsCubit`/`AuthCubit`). A fresh,
+/// `get_it`-factory-scoped instance per "+" tap (Boundaries: "Modal open
+/// resets") — starting state is always [TextEntryIdle] on
+/// [CaptureTab.texto] with empty text, so no explicit reset method is
+/// needed the way `AccountSettingsCubit.clearStaleError()` needs one for
+/// its own long-lived singleton.
+class TextEntryCubit extends Cubit<TextEntryState> {
+  TextEntryCubit(this._repository)
+    : super(const TextEntryIdle(activeTab: CaptureTab.texto, text: ''));
+
+  final EntriesRepository _repository;
+
+  /// Switches the active tab, preserving whatever Texto text was already
+  /// typed (Never: the full cross-tab cancel-safety rule is Story 3.4's
+  /// scope — this story's trivial case just needs the tab itself to
+  /// switch without losing in-progress text or firing any `create` call).
+  ///
+  /// Review finding: ignored while [TextEntrySaving] — `InsertionModal`
+  /// already disables the tab bar for that case, but this is the
+  /// authoritative guard regardless of how `selectTab` is invoked. Without
+  /// it, switching away mid-save would still let `save()`'s eventual
+  /// `TextEntrySaved`/`TextEntryError` emission land on top of whatever
+  /// tab/text the user has since moved to — popping the modal
+  /// unexpectedly, or showing an error against an unrelated tab.
+  void selectTab(CaptureTab tab) {
+    if (tab == state.activeTab || state is TextEntrySaving) {
+      return;
+    }
+    emit(TextEntryIdle(activeTab: tab, text: state.text));
+  }
+
+  /// Mirrors the Texto field's own `TextEditingController` into this
+  /// cubit's state, so [save] has the latest typed text to send. Ignored
+  /// while a save is already in flight — the field is disabled in that
+  /// state (`InsertionModal`), so this should never fire then regardless.
+  void updateText(String text) {
+    if (state is TextEntrySaving) {
+      return;
+    }
+    emit(TextEntryIdle(activeTab: state.activeTab, text: text));
+  }
+
+  /// I/O matrix's "Happy path save"/"Save fails" rows: fires `POST
+  /// /entries` with `source: manual` (Boundaries — the only source this
+  /// story ever sends) for whatever non-empty text is currently typed. A
+  /// blank/whitespace-only text never calls [EntriesRepository.create] —
+  /// `InsertionModal` already disables Salvar for that case, but this is
+  /// the authoritative guard regardless of how `save()` is invoked.
+  Future<void> save() async {
+    final text = state.text.trim();
+    if (text.isEmpty || state is TextEntrySaving) {
+      return;
+    }
+    final activeTab = state.activeTab;
+    emit(TextEntrySaving(activeTab: activeTab, text: text));
+    final result = await _repository.create(
+      content: text,
+      source: EntrySource.manual,
+    );
+    // Mirrors `AccountSettingsCubit.toggleBiometric`'s own guard: this
+    // cubit's `dispose:`/`close()` can race the awaited call above (e.g.
+    // the modal's barrier is dismissed mid-save) — `emit()` after `close()`
+    // would otherwise throw.
+    if (isClosed) {
+      return;
+    }
+    result.match(
+      (failure) => emit(
+        TextEntryError(activeTab: activeTab, text: text, message: failure.message),
+      ),
+      (_) => emit(TextEntrySaved(activeTab: activeTab, text: text)),
+    );
+  }
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,476 @@
+import 'dart:async';
+
+import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
+import 'package:flutter/semantics.dart';
+import 'package:flutter_bloc/flutter_bloc.dart';
+
+import '../../../../core/design_tokens.dart';
+import '../../../../core/widgets/app_button.dart';
+import '../cubit/text_entry_cubit.dart';
+
+/// The Insertion Modal — a 3-tab bottom sheet (Texto/Áudio/Foto) opened
+/// from the Home/Chat "+" control (`placeholder_screens.dart`). Only
+/// Texto is functional this story (Boundaries) — Áudio/Foto each render
+/// their own idle, non-interactive placeholder (Stories 3.2/3.3).
+class InsertionModal extends StatelessWidget {
+  const InsertionModal({required this.cubit, super.key});
+
+  final TextEntryCubit cubit;
+
+  /// Presents the modal exactly as the Boundaries dictate:
+  /// `showModalBottomSheet(isScrollControlled: true, barrierColor:
+  /// colorScrimHeavy)`, `radiusLg` top corners + `elevation2` (drawn by
+  /// this widget's own `Container`, not Material's `elevation` double —
+  /// same convention `ConfirmationDialog`'s card already uses), and a
+  /// `durationSheetUp` entrance that collapses to zero under Reduce
+  /// Motion (`MediaQuery.disableAnimations`).
+  ///
+  /// [cubit] is a fresh, `get_it`-factory-scoped instance — one per "+"
+  /// tap (Boundaries: "Modal open resets"), closed here once the sheet is
+  /// gone, regardless of how it closed (Salvar success, "x", swipe-down,
+  /// or barrier dismiss) — the caller never has to remember to do this
+  /// itself.
+  static Future<void> show(
+    BuildContext context, {
+    required TextEntryCubit cubit,
+  }) async {
+    final reduceMotion = MediaQuery.of(context).disableAnimations;
+    final controller =
+        BottomSheet.createAnimationController(Navigator.of(context))
+          ..duration = reduceMotion
+              ? Duration.zero
+              : DesignTokens.durationSheetUp
+          // Boundaries only names the entrance, but Reduce Motion should
+          // collapse the exit the same way — otherwise dismissing the
+          // sheet would still animate for anyone who asked for no motion.
+          ..reverseDuration = reduceMotion ? Duration.zero : null;
+    try {
+      await showModalBottomSheet<void>(
+        context: context,
+        isScrollControlled: true,
+        barrierColor: DesignTokens.colorScrimHeavy,
+        backgroundColor: Colors.transparent,
+        elevation: 0,
+        transitionAnimationController: controller,
+        builder: (_) => InsertionModal(cubit: cubit),
+      );
+    } finally {
+      // `showModalBottomSheet`'s own Future completes as soon as the
+      // route is popped — *before* the exit (`reverse()`) animation the
+      // framework drives on this same controller actually finishes.
+      // Disposing immediately would cancel that animation's ticker
+      // mid-flight, permanently freezing the sheet on screen (its
+      // `AnimatedBuilder` keeps rendering the controller's last value,
+      // and the route itself never reaches `AnimationStatus.dismissed`
+      // to be removed from the `Overlay`). Documented behavior
+      // (`BottomSheet.transitionAnimationController`'s own doc: "the
+      // caller is responsible for disposing it when the controller is
+      // no longer needed") — waiting for `dismissed` first is that
+      // "no longer needed" point.
+      if (!controller.isDismissed) {
+        final animationDone = Completer<void>();
+        void onStatusChange(AnimationStatus status) {
+          if (status == AnimationStatus.dismissed) {
+            animationDone.complete();
+          }
+        }
+
+        controller.addStatusListener(onStatusChange);
+        await animationDone.future;
+        controller.removeStatusListener(onStatusChange);
+      }
+      controller.dispose();
+      await cubit.close();
+    }
+  }
+
+  @override
+  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
+    return BlocProvider.value(value: cubit, child: const _InsertionModalBody());
+  }
+}
+
+class _InsertionModalBody extends StatefulWidget {
+  const _InsertionModalBody();
+
+  @override
+  State<_InsertionModalBody> createState() => _InsertionModalBodyState();
+}
+
+class _InsertionModalBodyState extends State<_InsertionModalBody> {
+  final _textController = TextEditingController();
+
+  /// Tracks the previously-seen `activeTab` so the listener can tell a
+  /// genuine tab switch apart from the many other `TextEntryIdle`
+  /// emissions a keystroke produces (`updateText` also emits `Idle`) —
+  /// initialized from the cubit's own current state so the very first
+  /// comparison (before any emission the listener sees) is still correct.
+  late CaptureTab _lastAnnouncedTab;
+
+  @override
+  void initState() {
+    super.initState();
+    _lastAnnouncedTab = context.read<TextEntryCubit>().state.activeTab;
+  }
+
+  @override
+  void dispose() {
+    _textController.dispose();
+    super.dispose();
+  }
+
+  // Labels for the 3 tabs, shared between the announcement below and
+  // `_TabBar`'s own rendering (`_TabBar._tabs`) — kept here too since
+  // `selectTab`'s announcement needs the label for whichever tab the
+  // user just switched *to*, not the cubit's own (enum-only) state.
+  static const _tabLabels = {
+    CaptureTab.texto: 'Texto',
+    CaptureTab.audio: 'Áudio',
+    CaptureTab.foto: 'Foto',
+  };
+
+  // Mirrors `account_settings_screen.dart`'s own `_announce` — VoiceOver
+  // (this app is iOS-only) doesn't reliably treat a live-region subtree
+  // update as an announcement on its own, so every state change this
+  // story introduces — saving, success, failure, and a tab switch — is
+  // spoken explicitly here instead (Acceptance Criteria: "no
+  // color/animation alone").
+  Future<void> _announce(String message) async {
+    if (!mounted) {
+      return;
+    }
+    await SemanticsService.sendAnnouncement(
+      View.of(context),
+      message,
+      TextDirection.ltr,
+    );
+  }
+
+  @override
+  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
+    return BlocConsumer<TextEntryCubit, TextEntryState>(
+      listener: (context, state) {
+        // Review finding: a tab switch (re-emitted as `TextEntryIdle`,
+        // same as every keystroke) previously went unannounced —
+        // detected here by comparing against the last tab seen, so a

+import 'package:fpdart/fpdart.dart';
+
+import '../../../../core/failure/failure.dart';
+import '../../../../core/network/api_client.dart';
+import '../../domain/entities/entry.dart';
+import '../models/entry_dto.dart';
+
+/// The entries feature's one write call so far (`entries-create`) — posts
+/// via the shared `ApiClient`, mirroring `account_remote_data_source.dart`'s
+/// pattern.
+class EntriesRemoteDataSource {
+  EntriesRemoteDataSource(this._apiClient);
+
+  final ApiClient _apiClient;
+
+  /// Sends exactly `{content, source}` — this story never passes
+  /// `chatMessageId`/`occurredAt`/`mediaDurationSeconds` (Boundaries: no
+  /// `Entry` field beyond the modeled 8; those three are optional in the
+  /// contract and belong to later stories/epics).
+  Future<Either<Failure, EntryDto>> create({
+    required String content,
+    required EntrySource source,
+  }) async {
+    final result = await _apiClient.post(
+      'entries-create',
+      data: {'content': content, 'source': source.name},
+    );
+    return result.flatMap((json) {
+      try {
+        final data = json['data'] as Map<String, dynamic>;
+        return right(EntryDto.fromJson(data));
+      } catch (error) {
+        // A 200 response that doesn't match the expected shape is a
+        // client-side parse failure, never a backend-sent code — maps to
+        // the local-only `malformedResponse` (RNF09: no exception escapes
+        // unmapped).
+        return left(Failure.malformedResponse(message: error.toString()));
+      }
+    });
+  }
+}

+import 'package:json_annotation/json_annotation.dart';
+
+import '../../domain/entities/entry.dart';
+
+part 'entry_dto.g.dart';
+
+/// `POST /entries`'s response `data` object (`openapi.yaml:370-456`) —
+/// decodes exactly the 8 fields [Entry] models (Code Map/Boundaries);
+/// every other field (`tags`/`piiStatus`/`piiSpans`/`embeddingStatus`/
+/// `mediaDurationSeconds`) is simply ignored by `json_serializable`'s
+/// generated `fromJson`, same convention `AccountSettingsDto` already
+/// uses for the fields it doesn't model.
+///
+/// [source] serializes/deserializes against [EntrySource]'s own `.name`
+/// (`json_serializable`'s default enum handling) — the enum's member
+/// names already match the backend's lowercase `manual`/`audio`/`photo`/
+/// `chat` strings exactly, so no `@JsonValue` overrides are needed.
+@JsonSerializable()
+class EntryDto {
+  const EntryDto({
+    required this.id,
+    required this.content,
+    required this.source,
+    required this.chatMessageId,
+    required this.occurredAt,
+    required this.serverRevision,
+    required this.createdAt,
+    required this.updatedAt,
+  });
+
+  final String id;
+  final String content;
+  final EntrySource source;
+  final String? chatMessageId;
+  final String occurredAt;
+  final int serverRevision;
+  final String createdAt;
+  final String updatedAt;
+
+  factory EntryDto.fromJson(Map<String, dynamic> json) =>
+      _$EntryDtoFromJson(json);
+
+  /// Also the exact shape written to the `entries` Hive box (Design
+  /// Notes: "raw `Map<String, dynamic>` via `EntryDto.toJson()`").
+  Map<String, dynamic> toJson() => _$EntryDtoToJson(this);
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,61 @@
+// The constructor keeps public named params (`remoteDataSource`,
+// `entriesBox`) distinct from the private fields they initialize, matching
+// `account_settings_repository_impl.dart`'s documented convention.
+// ignore_for_file: prefer_initializing_formals
+import 'package:fpdart/fpdart.dart';
+import 'package:hive_ce/hive_ce.dart';
+
+import '../../../../core/failure/failure.dart';
+import '../../domain/entities/entry.dart';
+import '../../domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart';
+import '../datasources/entries_remote_data_source.dart';
+import '../models/entry_dto.dart';
+
+/// On success, writes the entry through to the `entries` Hive box (`Box
+/// <Map>`, keyed by id, raw `EntryDto.toJson()` — Design Notes) *before*
+/// returning `right(...)`, same "persist then return" ordering
+/// `AuthRepositoryImpl._authenticate` already uses for its own
+/// post-success side effect.
+class EntriesRepositoryImpl implements EntriesRepository {
+  EntriesRepositoryImpl({
+    required EntriesRemoteDataSource remoteDataSource,
+    required Box<Map> entriesBox,
+  }) : _remoteDataSource = remoteDataSource,
+       _entriesBox = entriesBox;
+
+  final EntriesRemoteDataSource _remoteDataSource;
+  final Box<Map> _entriesBox;
+
+  @override
+  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> create({
+    required String content,
+    required EntrySource source,
+  }) async {
+    final result = await _remoteDataSource.create(
+      content: content,
+      source: source,
+    );
+    return result.match((failure) async => left(failure), (dto) async {
+      // A thrown Hive/disk exception must never escape unmapped (RNF09) —
+      // same rationale/fallback `AuthRepositoryImpl` already uses for its
+      // own local-persistence step.
+      try {
+        await _entriesBox.put(dto.id, dto.toJson());
+      } catch (error) {
+        return left(Failure.malformedResponse(message: error.toString()));
+      }
+      return right(_toEntry(dto));
+    });
+  }
+
+  Entry _toEntry(EntryDto dto) => Entry(
+    id: dto.id,
+    content: dto.content,
+    source: dto.source,
+    chatMessageId: dto.chatMessageId,
+    occurredAt: dto.occurredAt,
+    serverRevision: dto.serverRevision,
+    createdAt: dto.createdAt,
+    updatedAt: dto.updatedAt,
+  );
+}

+/// `POST /entries`'s four possible origins (`openapi.yaml:345-351`). This
+/// story only ever produces [manual] (Boundaries: "source=manual for this
+/// story") — the other three exist here already so the port
+/// ([EntriesRepository.create]) doesn't need to change shape when Stories
+/// 3.2/3.3 (audio/photo) and RF10 (chat) start passing them.
+enum EntrySource { manual, audio, photo, chat }
+
+/// A saved journal entry — plain `{id, content, source, chatMessageId,
+/// occurredAt, serverRevision, createdAt, updatedAt}` class, no `freezed`
+/// (mirrors `AuthenticatedUser`: this feature has no need for the
+/// union/copyWith machinery `Failure` uses). Boundaries: never a field
+/// beyond this exact set — `tags`/`piiStatus`/`piiSpans`/`embeddingStatus`/
+/// `mediaDurationSeconds` belong to later epics, not this story.
+///
+/// [occurredAt]/[createdAt]/[updatedAt] are kept as the backend's own ISO
+/// 8601 strings rather than parsed into `DateTime` — nothing in this story
+/// reads or formats them (Design Notes: the Hive box nothing reads from
+/// yet), so parsing would add risk (a malformed string throwing) with no
+/// behavior to justify it.
+class Entry {
+  const Entry({
+    required this.id,
+    required this.content,
+    required this.source,
+    required this.chatMessageId,
+    required this.occurredAt,
+    required this.serverRevision,
+    required this.createdAt,
+    required this.updatedAt,
+  });
+
+  final String id;
+  final String content;
+  final EntrySource source;
+
+  /// Non-null only for a [EntrySource.chat]-sourced entry (RF10) — always
+  /// `null` for this story's [EntrySource.manual] entries.
+  final String? chatMessageId;
+  final String occurredAt;
+  final int serverRevision;
+  final String createdAt;
+  final String updatedAt;
+
+  @override
+  bool operator ==(Object other) =>
+      identical(this, other) ||
+      (other is Entry &&
+          other.id == id &&
+          other.content == content &&
+          other.source == source &&
+          other.chatMessageId == chatMessageId &&
+          other.occurredAt == occurredAt &&
+          other.serverRevision == serverRevision &&
+          other.createdAt == createdAt &&
+          other.updatedAt == updatedAt);
+
+  @override
+  int get hashCode => Object.hash(
+    id,
+    content,
+    source,
+    chatMessageId,
+    occurredAt,
+    serverRevision,
+    createdAt,
+    updatedAt,
+  );
+
+  @override
+  String toString() =>
+      'Entry(id: $id, content: $content, source: $source, '
+      'chatMessageId: $chatMessageId, occurredAt: $occurredAt, '
+      'serverRevision: $serverRevision, createdAt: $createdAt, '
+      'updatedAt: $updatedAt)';
+}

+import 'package:fpdart/fpdart.dart';
+
+import '../../../../core/failure/failure.dart';
+import '../entities/entry.dart';
+
+/// The port later epics extend (Code Map) — this story gives it exactly
+/// one method, [create]. `features/capture/` depends on this abstract
+/// class only, never `entries/data` or `entries/presentation` (RNF06).
+abstract class EntriesRepository {
+  /// Posts to `entries-create` (`ApiClient.post`, via
+  /// `EntriesRemoteDataSource`) and, on success, writes the entry through
+  /// to the `entries` Hive box before returning `Right` (Boundaries) — a
+  /// caller that only reads the returned [Entry] never needs to touch the
+  /// box itself. Every [Failure] — including
+  /// [Failure.networkOffline] — is returned as `Left`, unmapped and
+  /// un-retried; the caller decides what to do with it (RNF09).
+  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> create({
+    required String content,
+    required EntrySource source,
+  });
+}

+import 'package:hive_ce/hive_ce.dart';

+import 'data/datasources/entries_remote_data_source.dart';

+import 'domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart';
+
+/// The `entries` Hive box's name — the first `hive_ce` box in the app
+/// (Code Map). A raw `Box<Map>`, not a generated `HiveObject`/
+/// `TypeAdapter` (Design Notes: avoids adapter codegen for a box nothing
+/// reads yet).
+const entriesBoxName = 'entries';
+
+/// Registers the `entries` feature into the project's single `get_it`
+/// instance (`sl`) — mirrors `features/account/account_injection.dart`'s
+/// pattern. Called from `setupCoreDependencies()` right after
+/// `Hive.initFlutter()` (Code Map), which must already have run by the
+/// time this opens its box.
+Future<void> registerEntriesFeature() async {
+  final entriesBox = await Hive.openBox<Map>(entriesBoxName);
+  sl.registerSingleton<Box<Map>>(entriesBox);
+
+  sl.registerLazySingleton<EntriesRemoteDataSource>(
+    () => EntriesRemoteDataSource(sl<ApiClient>()),
+  );
+
+  sl.registerLazySingleton<EntriesRepository>(
+    () => EntriesRepositoryImpl(
+      remoteDataSource: sl<EntriesRemoteDataSource>(),
+      entriesBox: sl<Box<Map>>(),
+    ),
+  );
+}

+import 'dart:async';
+
+import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';
+import 'package:fpdart/fpdart.dart';
+import 'package:mocktail/mocktail.dart';
+
+import 'package:cerne/core/failure/failure.dart';
+import 'package:cerne/features/capture/presentation/cubit/text_entry_cubit.dart';
+import 'package:cerne/features/entries/domain/entities/entry.dart';
+import 'package:cerne/features/entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart';
+
+class MockEntriesRepository extends Mock implements EntriesRepository {}
+
+const _savedEntry = Entry(
+  id: 'e1',
+  content: 'Hoje foi um bom dia.',
+  source: EntrySource.manual,
+  chatMessageId: null,
+  occurredAt: '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z',
+  serverRevision: 1,
+  createdAt: '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z',
+  updatedAt: '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z',
+);
+
+/// Covers spec-3-1's I/O & Edge-Case Matrix at the cubit layer:
+/// - "Modal open resets" -> a fresh cubit always starts `TextEntryIdle`
+///   on `CaptureTab.texto` with empty text.
+/// - "Happy path save" -> `TextEntrySaving` then `TextEntrySaved`, source
+///   always `manual`.
+/// - "Save fails (incl. offline)" -> `TextEntrySaving` then
+///   `TextEntryError` carrying `Failure.message` verbatim.
+/// - "Cancel before save" -> covered at the widget layer
+///   (`insertion_modal_test.dart`), since this cubit never calls `create`
+///   except from `save()`.
+void main() {
+  late MockEntriesRepository mockRepository;
+  late TextEntryCubit cubit;
+
+  setUpAll(() {
+    registerFallbackValue(EntrySource.manual);
+  });
+
+  setUp(() {
+    mockRepository = MockEntriesRepository();
+    cubit = TextEntryCubit(mockRepository);
+  });
+
+  tearDown(() => cubit.close());
+
+  test(
+    'starts TextEntryIdle on CaptureTab.texto with empty text (Boundaries: '
+    '"Opens on Texto, all 3 tabs idle/empty")',
+    () {
+      expect(
+        cubit.state,
+        isA<TextEntryIdle>()
+            .having((s) => s.activeTab, 'activeTab', CaptureTab.texto)
+            .having((s) => s.text, 'text', ''),
+      );
+    },
+  );
+
+  group('selectTab', () {
+    test('switches activeTab, preserving the current text', () {
+      cubit.updateText('rascunho');
+
+      cubit.selectTab(CaptureTab.audio);
+
+      expect(
+        cubit.state,
+        isA<TextEntryIdle>()
+            .having((s) => s.activeTab, 'activeTab', CaptureTab.audio)
+            .having((s) => s.text, 'text', 'rascunho'),
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('selecting the already-active tab is a no-op (no new emission)', () {
+      final emitted = <TextEntryState>[];
+      final subscription = cubit.stream.listen(emitted.add);
+
+      cubit.selectTab(CaptureTab.texto);
+
+      expect(emitted, isEmpty);
+      subscription.cancel();
+    });
+  });
+
+  group('updateText', () {
+    test('mirrors the typed text into state while idle', () {
+      cubit.updateText('um rascunho');
+
+      expect(cubit.state.text, 'um rascunho');
+      expect(cubit.state, isA<TextEntryIdle>());
+    });
+
+    test('ignored while a save is already in flight', () async {
+      final completer = Completer<Either<Failure, Entry>>();
+      when(
+        () => mockRepository.create(
+          content: any(named: 'content'),
+          source: any(named: 'source'),
+        ),
+      ).thenAnswer((_) => completer.future);
+      cubit.updateText('texto original');
+
+      final saveFuture = cubit.save();
+      cubit.updateText('tentativa de editar durante o save');
+
+      expect(cubit.state.text, 'texto original');
+
+      completer.complete(right(_savedEntry));
+      await saveFuture;
+    });
+  });
+
+  group('save() — happy path', () {
+    test(
+      'blank/whitespace-only text never calls create()',
+      () async {
+        cubit.updateText('   ');
+
+        await cubit.save();
+
+        verifyNever(
+          () => mockRepository.create(
+            content: any(named: 'content'),
+            source: any(named: 'source'),
+          ),
+        );
+        expect(cubit.state, isA<TextEntryIdle>());
+      },
+    );
+
+    test(
+      'non-empty text -> TextEntrySaving then TextEntrySaved, source '
+      'always manual (Boundaries)',
+      () async {
+        when(
+          () => mockRepository.create(
+            content: 'Hoje foi um bom dia.',
+            source: EntrySource.manual,
+          ),
+        ).thenAnswer((_) async => right(_savedEntry));
+        cubit.updateText('Hoje foi um bom dia.');
+
+        final emitted = <TextEntryState>[];
+        final subscription = cubit.stream.listen(emitted.add);
+
+        await cubit.save();
+        // Cubit's stream delivers via a microtask per emission — this
+        // drains the one still pending after `save()`'s own last `emit()`
+        // returns, same rationale
+        // `account_settings_repository_impl_test.dart`'s own
+        // `emittedDuring` helper already documents.
+        await Future<void>.delayed(Duration.zero);
+        await subscription.cancel();
+
+        expect(emitted, [isA<TextEntrySaving>(), isA<TextEntrySaved>()]);
+        verify(
+          () => mockRepository.create(
+            content: 'Hoje foi um bom dia.',
+            source: EntrySource.manual,
+          ),
+        ).called(1);
+      },
+    );
+  });
+
+  group('save() — failure (incl. offline)', () {
+    test(
+      'TextEntrySaving then TextEntryError carrying Failure.message '
+      'verbatim — modal stays open, no auto-retry',
+      () async {
+        when(
+          () => mockRepository.create(
+            content: any(named: 'content'),
+            source: any(named: 'source'),
+          ),
+        ).thenAnswer(
+          (_) async => left(const Failure.networkOffline(message: 'Sem conexão')),
+        );
+        cubit.updateText('Hoje foi um bom dia.');
+
+        final emitted = <TextEntryState>[];
+        final subscription = cubit.stream.listen(emitted.add);
+
+        await cubit.save();
+        await Future<void>.delayed(Duration.zero);
+        await subscription.cancel();
+
+        expect(emitted, [isA<TextEntrySaving>(), isA<TextEntryError>()]);
+        final errorState = cubit.state as TextEntryError;
+        expect(errorState.message, 'Sem conexão');
+        // Re-enabled: the text is preserved so the user can retry Salvar
+        // manually.
+        expect(errorState.text, 'Hoje foi um bom dia.');
+      },
+    );
+  });
+
+  test(
+    'emit() after close() never throws (a save racing a modal dismiss)',
+    () async {
+      final completer = Completer<Either<Failure, Entry>>();
+      when(
+        () => mockRepository.create(
+          content: any(named: 'content'),
+          source: any(named: 'source'),
+        ),
+      ).thenAnswer((_) => completer.future);
+      cubit.updateText('Hoje foi um bom dia.');
+
+      final saveFuture = cubit.save();
+      await cubit.close();
+      completer.complete(right(_savedEntry));
+
+      await expectLater(saveFuture, completes);
+    },
+  );
+}

  # Code Review Findings: Story 3.1 (Text Entry Capture & Insertion Modal Shell)
  
  - **Hive write-through failure after a successful backend create risks a duplicate server-side Entry.** In `lib/features/entries/data/repositories/entries_repository_impl.dart` (`create`, around line 30-43), if `_entriesBox.put(dto.id, dto.toJson())` throws *after* `_remoteDataSource.create` already succeeded (backend already persisted the Entry), the method returns `Left(Failure.malformedResponse(...))`. The cubit (`text_entry_cubit.dart`'s `save()`) treats this exactly like any other failure: it re-enables Salvar and keeps the typed text, inviting the user to retry. Since `POST /entries` for a `manual`-source entry has no idempotency key (the epic context notes idempotency only applies to `(origin, chatMessageId)`, relevant starting with RF10), a retry after this specific failure mode will fire a second `entries-create` call and create a duplicate Entry server-side. The existing test (`entries_repository_impl_test.dart`, "a Hive write failure maps to Left(malformedResponse)") proves the fallback mapping but never surfaces or addresses this downstream consequence.
  
  - **Raw exception text is surfaced verbatim as user-facing/announced copy.** Both `entries_remote_data_source.dart`'s parse-failure catch (`Failure.malformedResponse(message: error.toString())`) and `entries_repository_impl.dart`'s Hive-write catch do the same. That `message` becomes `TextEntryError.message`, which is shown inline in the Texto tab and spoken via `_announce(state.message)` in `insertion_modal.dart`. A user could see/hear something like `"Exception: disk full"` or a raw `FormatException` string instead of app-appropriate Portuguese copy — inconsistent with how every other mapped `Failure` in this codebase presumably carries a curated message.
  
  - **`_TabButton`'s `Semantics` wrapper risks double-announcing the tab label.** In `insertion_modal.dart`, `_TabButton` wraps `Semantics(button: true, selected: isActive, label: 'Aba $label', child: ... Text(label) ...)` with no `excludeSemantics: true`. Flutter does not automatically suppress a descendant widget's own implicit semantics (here, the inner `Text(label)`), so VoiceOver can announce both the explicit label ("Aba Texto") and the plain text node ("Texto") back-to-back. This is notable given this story's own emphasis on getting announced labels right ("never color/animation alone"). (`_CloseButton` doesn't have this issue since `Icon` carries no implicit label.)
  
  - **`TextField(maxLength: 20000, ...)` leaves Flutter's default character counter unaddressed.** In `_TextoTab` (`insertion_modal.dart`), no `counterText`/`buildCounter` override is supplied, so the Material default "0/20000" counter will render beneath the field by default. Nothing in the Design Notes, prototype extract, or `design_tokens.dart` accounts for this extra UI element, risking an unstyled/non-tokenized visual that technically falls outside the "every visual value lives in `design_tokens.dart`" discipline this project otherwise holds to.
  
  - **The success announcement races the modal's dismissal.** In `_InsertionModalBodyState`'s `BlocConsumer` listener, the `TextEntrySaved` case calls `_announce('Registro salvo')` without awaiting it, then immediately calls `Navigator.of(context).pop()`. The fire-and-forget platform-channel announcement can be superseded or interrupted by the subsequent screen-dismissal VoiceOver event triggered by the pop, with no test verifying the announcement actually survives this ordering on a real device.
  
  - **No announcement (or test) covers the modal's own initial appearance.** `_lastAnnouncedTab` is silently seeded from the cubit's current state in `initState`, so a screen-reader user opening the Insertion Modal never hears an explicit "Texto" announcement on open — only on a *later* tab switch. The behavior relies entirely on the platform's native modal-focus announcement, which is a reasonable bet but is an implicit, untested assumption given how deliberately every other transition in this file is announced.
  
  - **The generated `entry_dto.g.dart` is absent from the diff.** `lib/features/entries/data/models/entry_dto.dart` declares `part 'entry_dto.g.dart';`, but no such generated file appears anywhere in this changeset. Worth confirming this is genuinely gitignored consistent with the rest of the repo's generated-code convention (the diff never touches `Failure`'s existing freezed output either) rather than simply omitted — as submitted, the file can't compile standalone without running `build_runner`.
  
  - **`EntriesRemoteDataSource.create`'s catch block is too broad.** The `try`/`catch` around both `json['data'] as Map<String, dynamic>` and `EntryDto.fromJson(data)` (`entries_remote_data_source.dart`) will also swallow an unrelated `TypeError`/bug in totally different code reached from this block, mapping it indistinguishably to `malformedResponse` alongside a genuinely malformed backend payload — making a real client defect and a legitimate backend contract violation look identical in logs/telemetry.
  
  - **`sl.registerSingleton<Box<Map>>(entriesBox)` has no `instanceName`, and nothing in this story's own code guards against an accidental second registration.** `entries_injection.dart` registers the box keyed only by its bare generic type. While `deferred-work.md` already flags this for the *next* `hive_ce` consumer, it's also a live footgun today: any accidental duplicate `sl.registerSingleton<Box<Map>>(...)` call anywhere in this diff's own test setup would throw or silently shadow this registration, and nothing enforces/tests that this doesn't happen.
  
  - **Test coverage never exercises `EntrySource.audio`/`EntrySource.photo` through the actual network/datasource layer.** `entries_remote_data_source_test.dart` and `entries_repository_impl_integration_test.dart` cover `manual` and `chat` sources, but not `audio`/`photo`, even though `EntrySource` is explicitly widened now so Stories 3.2/3.3 can reuse this exact datasource method unchanged — leaving half of the enum's values unverified against real serialization/Hive round-tripping before those stories build on top of it.
  
  - **`_TextoTab.canSave` and the cubit's own save-guard are two independent sources of truth for "is there text to save."** `canSave` in `insertion_modal.dart` recomputes from `controller.text.trim().isNotEmpty` on every rebuild, while `TextEntryCubit.save()` independently re-derives `state.text.trim()`. These only stay in sync today because `onChanged` always re-emits cubit state in lockstep with the controller; nothing structurally prevents the two from drifting apart if either side is edited independently later.
  
  - **The "+" button resolves a `get_it` singleton inline from a core navigation widget.** `placeholder_screens.dart`'s FAB does `InsertionModal.show(context, cubit: sl<TextEntryCubit>())` directly inside `onPressed`, reaching into the global service locator from `lib/core/navigation/` rather than having the cubit handed in or resolved at a feature boundary — a minor architectural inconsistency with how DI resolution is otherwise scoped in this codebase.
</agent-message>

# Step 3: Triage

## RULES

- YOU MUST ALWAYS SPEAK OUTPUT in your Agent communication style with the config `{communication_language}`

## INSTRUCTIONS

1. **Normalize** findings from all layers into a unified list where each finding has:
   - `id` -- sequential integer
   - `source` -- the `id` of the layer that produced the finding (e.g., `blind-hunter`), or merged sources joined with `+` (e.g., `blind-hunter+edge-case-hunter`)
   - `title` -- one-line summary
   - `detail` -- full description
   - `location` -- file and line reference (if available)

2. **Deduplicate.** Deduplicate only findings with the same claim and same required action. If two or more findings meet both conditions, merge them into one:
   - Use the most specific finding as the base (prefer findings with a precise location over prose-only findings).
   - Append any unique detail, reasoning, or location references from the other finding(s) into the surviving `detail` field.
   - Set `source` to the merged sources (e.g., `blind-hunter+edge-case-hunter`).

3. Then evaluate each remaining finding independently. Do not reject a finding because a related finding was rejected.

4. **Read the code before rating.** Before assigning severity, open the source at each finding's location and read enough surrounding code to judge reachability -- call sites, guards, and validation that live outside the diff hunk. Do not rate from the diff hunk alone. Severity reflects the real consequence at a real call site, not the worst theoretical reading.

5. **Assign severity** to each finding by consequence for the artifact's main consumer (software user, document reader, etc).
   Disregard any severity assigned by a reviewing subagent. Review subagents operate under by-design information asymmetry and do not have enough context to set final severity for this workflow.
   - `low` -- none or cosmetic
   - `medium` -- tolerable
   - `high` -- intolerable

6. **Route** each finding into exactly one triage bucket:
   - **decision_needed** -- There is an ambiguous choice that requires human input. The code cannot be correctly patched without knowing the user's intent. Only possible if `{review_mode}` = `"full"`.
   - **patch** -- Code issue that is fixable without human input. The correct fix is unambiguous.
   - **defer** -- Pre-existing issue not caused by the current change. Real but not actionable now.
   - **dismiss** -- Noise, false positive, or handled elsewhere.

   If `{review_mode}` = `"no-spec"` and a finding would otherwise be `decision_needed`, reclassify it as `patch` (if the fix is unambiguous) or `defer` (if not).

7. **Drop** all `dismiss` findings. Record the dismiss count for the summary.

8. If `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, report which layers failed before announcing results. If zero findings remain after dropping dismissed AND `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, warn the user that the review may be incomplete rather than announcing a clean review.

9. If zero findings remain after triage (all rejected or none raised): state "✅ Clean review — all layers passed." (Step 3 already warned if any review layers failed via `{failed_layers}`.)

## NEXT

Read fully and follow `./step-04-present.md`

3	part 'failure.freezed.dart';
4	
5	/// AD-3 — the one closed `Failure` hierarchy, exactly 14 subtypes: the 13
6	/// codes from `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md` plus the local-only
7	/// `malformedResponse` (client-side parse failure, never sent by the
8	/// backend). Never redefined or subset per feature; every repository method
9	/// returns `Either<Failure, T>` built from this type (RNF09).
10	///
11	/// `retryable` is derived here, once, from the 6 server `retryable:true`
12	/// codes (AD-4) — no other file re-decides which codes retry.
13	@freezed
14	sealed class Failure with _$Failure {
15	  const factory Failure.authExpired({required String message}) = AuthExpired;
16	  const factory Failure.authInvalid({required String message}) = AuthInvalid;
17	  const factory Failure.networkTimeout({required String message}) =
18	      NetworkTimeout;
19	  const factory Failure.networkOffline({required String message}) =
20	      NetworkOffline;
21	  const factory Failure.validation({required String message}) = Validation;
22	  const factory Failure.piiCheckFailed({required String message}) =
23	      PiiCheckFailed;
24	  const factory Failure.embeddingFailed({required String message}) =
25	      EmbeddingFailed;
26	  const factory Failure.aiGenerationTimeout({required String message}) =
27	      AiGenerationTimeout;
28	  const factory Failure.notFound({required String message}) = NotFound;
29	  const factory Failure.rateLimited({required String message}) = RateLimited;
30	  const factory Failure.exportEmptyPeriod({required String message}) =
31	      ExportEmptyPeriod;
32	  const factory Failure.payloadTooLarge({required String message}) =
33	      PayloadTooLarge;
34	  const factory Failure.ocrNoText({required String message}) = OcrNoText;
35	
36	  /// Local-only — the client's own parse-failure detection. `retryable` is
37	  /// hardcoded `false` for this subtype (AD-3).
38	  const factory Failure.malformedResponse({required String message}) =
39	      MalformedResponse;
40	
41	  const Failure._();
42	
43	  /// The 6 server `retryable:true` codes (AD-4). Every other code —
44	  /// including the local `malformedResponse` — is `false`.
45	  bool get retryable => switch (this) {
46	        NetworkTimeout() => true,
47	        NetworkOffline() => true,
48	        PiiCheckFailed() => true,
49	        EmbeddingFailed() => true,
50	        AiGenerationTimeout() => true,
51	        RateLimited() => true,
52	        AuthExpired() ||
53	        AuthInvalid() ||
54	        Validation() ||
55	        NotFound() ||
56	        ExportEmptyPeriod() ||
57	        PayloadTooLarge() ||
58	        OcrNoText() ||
59	        MalformedResponse() =>
60	          false,
61	      };
62	
63	  /// Maps a backend error `code` (`error-taxonomy.md`) to its `Failure`
64	  /// subtype. An unrecognized code (should never happen — the taxonomy is
65	  /// closed) falls back to [Failure.malformedResponse] rather than throwing,
66	  /// so no repository ever lets an unmapped error escape (RNF09).
67	  factory Failure.fromCode(String code, String message) => switch (code) {
68	        'AUTH_EXPIRED' => Failure.authExpired(message: message),
69	        'AUTH_INVALID' => Failure.authInvalid(message: message),
70	        'NETWORK_TIMEOUT' => Failure.networkTimeout(message: message),
71	        'NETWORK_OFFLINE' => Failure.networkOffline(message: message),
72	        'VALIDATION_ERROR' => Failure.validation(message: message),
73	        'PII_CHECK_FAILED' => Failure.piiCheckFailed(message: message),
74	        'EMBEDDING_FAILED' => Failure.embeddingFailed(message: message),
75	        'AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT' =>
76	          Failure.aiGenerationTimeout(message: message),
77	        'NOT_FOUND' => Failure.notFound(message: message),
78	        'RATE_LIMITED' => Failure.rateLimited(message: message),
79	        'EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD' => Failure.exportEmptyPeriod(message: message),
80	        'PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE' => Failure.payloadTooLarge(message: message),
81	        'OCR_NO_TEXT' => Failure.ocrNoText(message: message),
82	        _ => Failure.malformedResponse(message: message),
83	      };
84	}

23	  /// this widget's own `Container`, not Material's `elevation` double —

32	  /// itself.

45	          // sheet would still animate for anyone who asked for no motion.
